title: Minimize instrumentation overhead by introducing adaptive harvester
creator: Leah Park
description: We are seeing higher CPU and memory pressure across the inference runtime clusters attributable to our default instrumentation. The goal of this ticket is to introduce an adaptive harvester component that reduces per-request telemetry work by dynamically switching between full and lightweight collection modes based on runtime load and request SLOs. This will also add a zero-copy span bridge for hot-path spans and a lightweight log-emitter path for short-lived worker processes. The work reduces tail-latency regression risk introduced by tracing, lowers observability cost, and creates a clear knobset for production operators.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive harvester deployed to canary and running on at least 3% of traffic with no increase in 99th percentile token latency
CPU utilization attributable to instrumentation on busy nodes reduced by >= 25% in synthetic load tests
No loss of critical trace/span relationships for sampled traces (end-to-end test)
Rollout plan and automated rollback in the console are documented and validated
technical_notes: Adaptive harvester: separate worker that subscribes to runtime signals (queue depth, latency SLO breach counters) and flips telemetry mode via a small shared config; avoids per-request decision logic in hot path
Zero-copy span bridge: use pre-allocated fixed-size buffers and pointer handoff to the async span writer to avoid temporary allocations on span start/finish
Lightweight log-emitter: fall back to line-oriented, non-json logs for short-lived processes to reduce serialization cost; keep structured logs for services with high retention requirements
Sampling policy: introduce route-aware sampling with higher fidelity for customer-facing routes and aggressive head-based sampling for internal or high-throughput routes
Compatibility: OTLP export remains unchanged; harvester annotates fewer fields when in lightweight mode to preserve downstream schema expectations
tasks: Prototype adaptive harvester daemon and local mode toggle
Benchmark baseline and prototype under synthetic workloads (latency, cpu, memory)
Implement zero-copy span bridge in runtime agent and integrate with async exporter
Add route-aware sampling configuration and admin API to toggle per-service policies
Canary rollout to staging clusters -> monitor p99 latency, export rate, CPU-tagged metrics
Document operator runbook and console toggle for rollout/rollback
